title: Met32's Role in Methionine Biosynthesis in C. albicans
summary: This cluster revolves around Met32, a gene or protein that plays a crucial role in methionine biosynthesis in Candida albicans. Met32 has genes in both C. albicans and its met32 mutant strain, and it regulates the expression of several other genes, including Sod1 and Ssu1. Met32 also interacts with Met4 and binds to several other proteins, including JLP11, SOA1, and Seo13. The cluster also includes other genes and proteins involved in methionine biosynthesis, such as MET15 and Met31, as well as the organism C. albicans and its met32 mutant strain. The cluster also mentions the import of GSH into C. albicans and Francisella novicida, but this is not directly related to Met32's role in methionine biosynthesis.
